title: Docs-site snippet retirement and translation playbook
author: Priya Raman
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the process, roles, and technical patterns our Developer Experience (DX) team uses to retire, update, and translate code snippets, API examples, and small how-tos that appear across the docs site, SDK guides, quickstarts, and API reference. It is intended for documentation owners, SDK maintainers, localization partners, and support engineers who propagate canonical fixes into documentation and SDK examples.

Goals:
- Ensure snippet changes are safe, discoverable, and reversible.
- Reduce stale or broken examples across languages by centralizing lifecycle rules.
- Provide a clear translation/localization workflow so localized pages are updated in step with English source edits.
- Maintain a fast path for urgent canonical fixes coming from support/triage.

Scope (what this playbook covers):
- Single-file snippets embedded in docs, quickstarts, and API examples.
- Language variants (python, javascript, curl) of the same example.
- Snippet metadata, tagging, and canonical source references.
- CI checks that verify snippet compilation or linter rules where possible.

Out of scope:
- Full sample applications (these follow the SDK repo release lifecycle).
- API surface changes that require SDK releases (those coordinate with Engineering Change Control).

Key definitions:
- Canonical snippet: the primary source snippet maintained in the docs repo (usually under /snippets/).
- Snippet retirement: a formal removal or replacement of a snippet because it is obsolete, insecure, or replaced by a better pattern.
- Localized page: a translated doc page that mirrors an English source.

Owners & roles:
| Role | Responsibility | Primary contact |
|------|----------------|-----------------|
| Docs owner | Proposes snippet retirement/changes; writes replacement guidance | Priya Raman |
| SDK maintainer | Verifies language samples and raises SDK backport PRs if required | Ethan Morales |
| Localization lead | Coordinates translation updates and timing | Sofia Klein |
| Support escalation | Triggers urgent canonical-fix pathway when snippets cause customer impact | Daniel Park |
| Release coordinator | Approves scheduled doc deploy windows and notifies downstream teams | ReleaseOps Team |

Governance & approval thresholds:
- Minor fixes (typos, formatting, linter fixes): Docs owner can merge after single reviewer sign-off.
- Behavioral fixes (auth change, example that could produce incorrect results): Docs owner + SDK maintainer must approve.
- Retirement of major example patterns (e.g., removing OAuth snippet): Docs owner + SDK lead + Security review required.

Snippet metadata standard (required front-matter for any canonical snippet):
- id: short-handle (e.g. embed-quickstart-python)
- languages: comma-separated (python,javascript,curl)
- status: canonical | deprecated | retired | experimental
- last_reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD
- owner: team-or-person

Example front-matter (YAML):
---
# id: embed-quickstart-python
languages: python,javascript,curl
status: canonical
last_reviewed: 2026-02-10
owner: eng-devx
---

Retirement workflow (recommended cadence: quarterly review for low-risk snippets, immediate for critical fixes):
1) Proposal: Docs owner raises a Snippet Retirement RFC in the docs repo as a PR to /snippets/ with the reason and proposed replacement (if any).
2) Impact analysis: Include a quick search report (grep/graph) listing pages that reference the snippet. Use the internal snippet index: /docs/snippet-index.csv.
3) Classification: Mark the PR as one of: minor, breaking, security. If breaking or security, add label `retire-breaking` or `retire-security`.
4) Review: Required reviewers per classification (see Governance above). Add localized pages to reviewers.
5) Canary deploy: Merge to `canary-docs` and verify CI checks pass (compilation, snippet linters). Notify QA channel.
6) Observability window: Keep the change in canary for 48 hours and collect telemetry: 404s for removed snippet IDs, feedback form hits, and support tickets referencing the example.
7) Full rollout: Schedule to main docs deploy window. Communicate change in the weekly docs digest and to SDK teams.
8) Archive: Move retired snippet file to /snippets/retired/YYYYMMDD-<id>.md and update snippet-index.csv.

Urgent canonical fix pathway (support-driven):
- Trigger: Support files a P1 if a snippet causes incorrect behavior in customer production flows (e.g., auth header example that leaks tokens).
- Steps:
  1. Support posts a ticket in #docs-urgent with reference and suggested patch.
  2. Docs owner creates an emergency PR titled `URGENT: canonical fix <id>` and adds `emergency` label.
  3. At least one SDK maintainer validates the fix (this can be a lightweight smoke test).
  4. PR merged to `canary-docs` and released to `main` with override per ReleaseOps policy (no wait window).
  5. Postmortem: owner documents cause and preventive action in the PR.

Translation / localization workflow (synchronization strategy):
- Principle: Localized pages must not lag behind canonical safety fixes. For retirements and security fixes, localized pages must be updated within 7 calendar days.
- Process:
  1) Mark the English PR with label `i18n-update-required` and add a `translation-delta` note in the PR description describing the scope of change.
  2) Localization lead triggers a translation job and assigns translators with a 72-hour SLA for minor textual edits; 7 days for behavioral changes.
  3) Localized PRs should reference the English canonical PR in their description (link to original PR).
  4) If localized content cannot be updated in time for the main deployment (e.g., legal constraints), the English change can be blocked only by Security/Legal; otherwise we proceed and add a localized warning banner automatically using the i18n pipeline.

Snippet tagging, CI and automated checks:
- All snippets must pass automated linters for the language and a lightweight snippet-checker. For languages we support, we run:
  - python: flake8 + snippet-run (virtualenv + run)
  - javascript: eslint + node-run-check
  - curl: http request smoke test (where endpoint public or mocked)

Sample GitHub Actions job (snippet smoke check):
name: snippet-smoke-checks
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  python-snippets:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'
      - name: Run snippet runner
        run: |
          pip install -r tools/snippet-check/requirements.txt
          python tools/snippet-check/run_snippets.py --language python --path snippets/

Propagating canonical fixes to SDK guides and API examples (checklist):
- Create accompanying SDK issue/PR if the change requires an SDK release (auth flows, method names).
- If no SDK code change is required, update SDK guide pages with note: "Updated to reflect docs canonical fix <PR link>".
- Coordinate with SDK maintainers for backports if older major versions require the same fix.
- Add a `support-canonicalized` tag to the support ticket.

Support & canonical fixes triage matrix:
- Severity P0/P1: use urgent pathway.
- Severity P2: schedule within 3 business days.
- Severity P3: normal triage (next sprint).

QA checklist before merge:
- [ ] Snippet front-matter present and valid.
- [ ] Linter checks pass for all languages in `languages` front-matter.
- [ ] Impact analysis attached (pages list).
- [ ] Localization impact flagged if present.
- [ ] If security-sensitive, security review attached.

Monitoring & metrics to track success:
- Count of retired snippets per quarter (goal: reduce stale snippet backlog by 50% YoY).
- Number of support tickets referencing snippet examples (goal: 0 for high-severity cases).
- Time-to-fix for emergency canonical fixes (SLA target: < 4 hours for detection-to-canary-merge).

Rollback & recovery procedure:
1) Revert PR in the docs repo and deploy to canary.
2) Run snippet smoke checks and open communication in #docs-ops with timeline.
3) If revert fails, contact ReleaseOps to block the main deploy and escalate to Eng SRE.

Examples & migration notes (common scenarios):
- Replacing API key header with short-lived token pattern: classify as `breaking` and add Security reviewer.
- Removing deprecated method: mark snippet `deprecated` first, keep for one release cycle, then retire.
- Example requiring SDK change: open SDK issue and label `docs-blocker`; docs PR should link to SDK PR.

References and useful links:
- /docs/snippet-index.csv (internal)
- Docs deploy windows calendar (shared Google calendar link)
- SDK repo contribution guidelines
- Internal support canonical-fix playbook (sops)

FAQ (short):
Q: What if a localized translation causes functional drift?
A: Localized pages have the same responsibility as English. When functional drift is detected, the localized page should be reverted and a translation correction PR opened referencing the original fix.

Q: Can I retire a snippet without replacement?
A: Yes, but provide migration guidance in the PR and update the referencing pages to point to the recommended alternative.

Q: Who approves a security-sensitive snippet change?
A: Docs owner + SDK maintainer + Security review.
